messages:
lina: Heads-up — planning an envelope refresh run across several buckets to replace legacy KEKs with new customer-scoped KEKs. need quick eyes on perms + audit shape.

tom: how aggressive is the plan? concurrency / qps targets? we don't want huge s3/list-object churn.

lina: start low: 20 threads per region, target 50 items/s steady total, exponential backoff on 429s.

devops: suggest token-bucket limiter per-worker + global cap. make chunk size configurable.

arjun: note: AWS KMS has GenerateDataKey/Decrypt latencies ~10-50ms, GCP KMS is a bit higher for remote calls. recommend batching envelope ops and minimizing roundtrips.

kate: we also need clear progress checkpoints so we can resume if a pod dies. manifest with last_processed_key and per-shard offsets.

tom: agree. manifest entries: shard_id, last_key, bytes_scanned, errors_count. write s3://redwood-kms-refresh/manifests/{run_ts}/{shard}.json atomically.

security-bot: Reminder: any key operations must emit audit events to central logging within 30s and include principal, kek_id, envelope_id, operation, result. See policy 3.2.

lina: good call. add structured audit: <principal>, <source>, <old_kek>, <new_kek>, <object_key>, <status>. keep PII out.

arjun: for GCP, ensure service account has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the new key ring and also viewer on projects to list keys. For AWS, attach kms:Decrypt,kms:GenerateDataKey to the instance role and grant via resource policy if cross-account.

devops: about throttling — implement per-key backoff. if a specific object fails more than 3x with KMS rate/limit, push to dead-letter store s3://.../dlq/{run_ts}/.json and continue.

kate: DLQ should include full audit context + last error. add a monitoring alert for >100 dlq items in 1h.

tom: make all operations idempotent. use compare-and-swap on object metadata: set metadata.refresh_epoch = run_ts when successful; skip if already >= run_ts.

lina: sample check snippet we can run from a worker: ```
# check object metadata
aws s3api head-object --bucket X --key path/to/object | jq '.Metadata'
```

arjun: envelope format notes: we use v2 envelopes: "v2|kek:<kek_id>|alg:AES-256-GCM|wrap:<base64>" — keep parser tolerant to unknown fields.

devops: recovery plan: job writes manifest every minute, a controller watches manifests and can reassign shards. if controller restarts, it reclaims un-updated shards after lease TTL 2m.

security-bot: Add audit entries for shard reassignment events too. reassignments are sensitive.

kate: regarding rollback: we should preserve original envelope as metadata.old_envelope_ref and not delete until 7 days after run completion. gives us a fallback.

lina: agreed. retention window 7d, then cleanup job can purge. include a toggle to skip retention for test runs.

tom: small perf note — prefetch object lists with continuation tokens and feed to workers via a local queue, don't let workers call list-object directly. reduces API spikes.

arjun: also consider using KMS in-project keys for bulk operations where possible to reduce cross-account latency. for cross-account, consider a short-lived grant instead of full IAM binding.

devops: add metrics: envelopes_processed_total, envelopes_failed_total, dlq_size, avg_kms_latency_ms, manifest_write_latency_ms. push to datadog.

lina: action items: (1) arjun draft IAM/role playbook for AWS/GCP (2) devops prototype limiter + manifest pattern (3) security team to confirm audit schema (4) kate instrument DLQ alerting.

kate: i'll own the DLQ alerting + retention policy.

arjun: I'll put together the IAM snippets and a short runbook for creating short-lived grants.

devops: I'll spin a small POC that runs against a staging bucket with throttling knobs.

security-bot: Logged: security/ops ticket #SEC-7732 created for audit schema review.

lina: thanks all — will schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to review the POC. :thumbsup:
